raw_segments.text: But in the drawing room, the conversation was already over.
Katarina Ivanovna was greatly excited, though she looked resolute.
At the moment Alyosha and Madame Holikov entered, Ivan Fyodorovich stood up to take leave.
His face was rather pale, and Alyosha looked at him anxiously.
For this moment was to solve a doubt, a harassing enigma which had for some time haunted Alyosha.
During the preceding month, it had been several times suggested to him that his brother Ivan
was in love with Katarina Ivanovna, and, what was more, that he meant to carry her
off from Dmitry.
Until quite lately the idea seemed to Alyosha monstrous, though it worried him extremely.
He loved both his brothers, and dreaded such rivalry between them.
Meantime, Dmitry had said outright on the previous day that he was glad that Ivan was
his rival, and that it was a great assistance to him, Dmitry.
In what way did it assist him?
To marry Grashenko.
But that Alyosha considered the worst thing possible.
Besides all this, Alyosha had till the evening before implicitly believed that Katarina Ivanovna
had a steadfast and passionate love for Dmitry, but he had only believed it till the evening
before.
He had fancied, too, that she was incapable of loving a man like Ivan, and that she did
love Dmitry, and loved him just as he was, in spite of all the strangeness of such a
passion.
